highlights_headline: SkiaSharp 4.159 introduces an experimental image-comparison package for testing rendered output.
highlights_body: The upcoming release also adjusts Ganesh texture-edge sampling and Tizen CPU blur selection. Linux x86 native assets will no longer be included.

breaking.title: Move Linux x86 deployments to a supported architecture
breaking.body: Linux x86 native assets will no longer be included in NuGet packages, following upstream .NET's removal of Linux x86 cross-build infrastructure. Move 32-bit x86 Linux deployments to a supported architecture before upgrading.

bullets.detail: SkiaSharp.Testing adds SKImageComparison for images, bitmaps and pixmaps, with channel tolerances, masks, mismatch budgets, error metrics and difference images. The separately packaged assembly is experimental: opt in by suppressing SKIA4001 with NoWarn or a pragma. Comparison results retain no native handles; returned difference images belong to the caller.

bullets.lead: Keep filtered texture samples inside subset edges
bullets.detail: Ganesh bilinear texture sampling now clamps slightly inward to avoid including undefined texels outside a subset. Texture-edge pixels may change; CPU and Graphite rendering are unaffected.

Tizen now applies its intended blur configuration to Skia itself, selecting the existing ThreeBoxApprox/Tent path instead of the shader-based Gaussian candidate. Blur pixels and performance may differ; Tizen rendering and performance were not measured locally.

contributor_summaries.ramezgerges: Restored the Uno Gallery and its view projects to the Windows samples solution.
